Once an unremarkable island known for sunset-hued salt marshes and Tassel Jellies, it changed when the heaviest fragment of the fallen moonstone crashed on its shores. It is now a staging ground for Fatui personnel in Nod-Krai, who work from the huge Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau, and it also holds the Lightkeepers' abandoned Final Night Cemetery.

The two halves of the island contrast: a cold steel Fatui installation that dominates the landscape as a statement of power, and a lonely lighthouse outpost lit by a single Lightkeeper who looks after the dead.

Geography: Paha Isle is the island south of Voidsea Outlook across the water, part of the Southern Isles with Lempo Isle and Hiisi Island. The Design Bureau is a colossal structure of iron and stone built by the Fatui; the Final Night Cemetery lies around a lighthouse on the island. Local specialty: Frostlamp Flower.

Places: Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau: the Fatui's high-tech complex. Final Night Cemetery: the former Lightkeeper outpost, lighthouse and burial ground, always dark.

People: The Fatui soldiers of the Bureau, including the Poruchik Raskolnikov, who oversees it. Flins, a Ratnik, lives alone at the lighthouse. Ghosts of dead Lightkeepers remain, among them the Loud Phantom (Dietrich), the Ritual-Conducting Phantom and, after The Chef's Tale, the Food-Obsessed Phantom (Jaakob).

Governance: The Bureau is run by Fatui personnel under Raskolnikov for maintaining order and efficiency. The cemetery has no authority: the Lightkeepers abandoned the island and Flins remains stationed there on his own.

History: Several decades ago the light of the historic Lightkeeper outpost was snuffed out in a conflict against the Wild Hunt, and ninety percent of the troops stationed there died. In despair the Ratniki turned to the legendary 'blue lantern', and by coincidence awakened Flins, who helped them fight despite his weakness at that moment. The survivors and Flins buried the fallen and founded the cemetery; the Lightkeepers then left, and only Flins remained.

Atmosphere: Two moods: the Bureau, cold metal, alarms and the sense of being watched; the cemetery, a dark island with one signalling light, lonely graves and the ghosts of dead Lightkeepers.

Dangers: Fatui patrols in the Bureau (Oprichniki Line Troopers, Support Troopers, Medics, Vanguards and Grenadiers, among others), alarm systems that call in reinforcements, and the boss Super-Heavy Landrover: Mechanized Fortress. After the quest Raskolnikov can be fought again as a Local Legend.

Quests: The Shoemaker's Children Go Barefoot (world quest, chapter East of the Moon, West of the Sun): the Traveler enters the Bureau, meets the girl Netochka, and fights through Fatui to Raskolnikov; completing it unlocks him as a Local Legend. To the Lighthouse (world quest): the Traveler fuels and lights the lighthouse in the Final Night Cemetery with Flins; it leads to The Special Support Squad's Tale.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the island remains open to explore, with the Fatui complex still standing and Flins posted at the cemetery.

Nothing in 7.0-7.1 is recorded as changing the island.

144.comment: Paha Isle: Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau
144.content: A colossal steel structure erected by the Fatui, its bulk dominating the ancient landscape as a declaration of power and control. It serves as the Fatui staging ground in Nod-Krai and is run by the Poruchik Raskolnikov.

145.content: Home of Flins and of the ghosts of dead Lightkeepers, built around an old outpost lighthouse whose light was never extinguished until a Wild Hunt battle killed most of its garrison. It is always dark. The Meeting Point is at the lighthouse.

146.content: Poruchik of the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau, a quest NPC. He is strict, and he respects strength, such as Stalanov's and the Traveler's. He considers Netochka arrogant.

147.content:
Path of Misery (also: Beneath Kipumaki): The Path of Misery is a large winding cavern under Kipumaki Cliff in Ashveil Peak, in far northern Nod-Krai. It funnels down into the Chasm of Endless Decay, the pit where the Abyssal Scourge of Endless Decay was sealed five hundred years ago and where it was finally destroyed in the world quest When War Songs Rise.

The wiki's map shows two levels, Beneath Kipumaki and the Path of Misery itself, and the cavern shares its music with the Chasm. It is thin canon: most of what is known about the place comes from the Chasm, the cliff above, and the quest that ends there.

Geography: Beneath Kipumaki Cliff, in Ashveil Peak, the northernmost part of Pohjola. It is a winding cave that narrows and descends into the Chasm of Endless Decay. Kipumaki Cliff above it is shrouded in dark clouds and subject to Abyssal Decay, a climate effect that drains health from those in it unless they shelter near Oath Lanterns.

History: Five hundred years ago, the Torchforger Solovei and the first Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions, Aila, with the help of Alia, subdued the Scourge of Endless Decay and sealed it beneath Kipumaki Cliff with a sealing array. The area afterwards became a hotspot of Wild Hunt activity, and the Lightkeepers set up Cliffwatch Camp to watch it.

Dangers: Wild Hunt creatures and Abyssal enemies fill the area, and Abyssal Decay accumulates steadily near the Chasm; in the quest the Traveler cannot reduce it for a time and recovers health by dispelling Abyssal shadows. Illusions of fallen Lightkeepers appear in the fog.

Atmosphere: Fog, creeping dark and a sense of being watched. In the quest the air grows thicker as Illuga approaches, and the fallen seem to speak from the fog as illusions. The area's themes on the wiki are The Forlorn Trek of Suffering and The Soul-Devouring Nightmare.

Travel: Reached from Kipumaki Cliff. Completing When War Songs Rise unlocks a teleport waypoint at the Chasm of Endless Decay.

Quests: When War Songs Rise (World Quest, Nightingale's Song, Act II: Darradarljod) sees the Traveler help Illuga and the Nightmare Orioles rebuild the sealing barrier at Kipumaki Cliff and fight off the Scourge, then Illuga goes alone after it into its lair, with the Traveler and his squad joining him. Using the Spiralblade they kill the Scourge and cleanse the area of its influence.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Scourge of Endless Decay is destroyed and the Chasm and its approach are explorable. The wiki notes the area is cleansed of its influence. Nothing after 7.1 is recorded.

148.comment: Path of Misery: Path of Misery
148.content: The Path of Misery is a large winding cavern under Kipumaki Cliff that leads into the Chasm of Endless Decay, where the Scourge of Endless Decay was sealed and later destroyed. Fog and Abyssal shadows haunt the descent.

149.content:
Pillar of Embla (also: Embla Pillar, Tower Piercing at the Sky): The Pillar of Embla is a great divine pillar in Wavechaser Plain in northern Nod-Krai, rooted in the earth and rising toward the sky. It was raised about five hundred years ago, during the Cataclysm, by Rauthvangi (known at the Belyi Tsar's court as Rotwang) as a tower to reach the false sky and carry him to his "Elysium", the Abyss. In the centuries since, its presence has permanently altered the surrounding land.

In recent events it became the site of the Lightkeepers' effort to stop Rotwang's return. The Frostmoon Scions remember that their first Moonchanter, Aila, travelled to it at the request of the Torchforger Solovei to end the Abyssal catastrophe he caused.

Geography: The Pillar stands in Wavechaser Plain, in the north of Nod-Krai, within reach of the Lightkeepers' city of Piramida. Wild plants and creatures of the Nod-Krai wilds grow around it, among them mandragora, spirebloom, cottonspring flowers, glimmerfruit and slothsheep; winter icelea is gathered here, and Moonlane is also found in the area. The loading-screen text calls it a divine pillar "firmly rooted in the earth and reaching skyward".

History: Rauthvangi was a Khaenri'ahn scholar-monk exiled for his obsession with the Abyss, which he called the pitch-black Elysium. He reached Nod-Krai when it was still a barren borderland, later served the Belyi Tsar as the alchemist Rotwang, and built the Pillar of Embla as a tower to break through the false sky and open the way for the Abyss. Aila and Solovei stopped the first attempt; Rotwang rose again but was sealed at Kipumaki Cliff.

Quests: Tower of Inversion (Nightingale's Song, Prelude to the Night Vigil, Part 2) starts at the Pillar of Embla: the Traveler and Illuga enter the tower, clear it, purify the Abyssal core and activate a barrier core. It leads into When War Songs Rise.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Pillar of Embla is open to exploration. Rotwang's threat from it was ended in the Nightingale's Song chapter.

The Calamity Egg that formed around the pillar was destroyed. The state of the structure afterwards is not described in the sources read.

150.comment: Pillar of Embla: Aila at the Pillar of Embla
150.content: According to the Frostmoon Scions' records, as told by Verna, Aila went to the Pillar of Embla in northern Nod-Krai at Solovei's request and "put an end to the Abyssal catastrophe" caused by Rauthvangi.

151.comment: Pillar of Embla: Ratnik Diaries at Kipumaki Cliff
151.content: At the pillar is the first of three connected diary entries by a new Ratnik named Filaev. He was selected as the last name on the Ratniki list, proud of his uniform and personalised lantern, then assigned to a support unit at Kipumaki Cliff under Captain Asebov with Chernov, Shonokovych (a former poet) and Patolichev. After months of routine he was excited when Piramida ordered the unit to clear Wild Hunt nests around the cliff, expecting his first battle. The continuation appears at the Sanctum of Departed Heroes.

152.content:
Piramida: Piramida is the city of the Lightkeepers, Nod-Krai's volunteer militia against the Wild Hunt. It stands on a mountain around a giant golden-age lighthouse and is a garrison town of Ratniki: soldiers' lodgings, an infirmary, a forge, a plaza with a bulletin board, a great mead hall at the top, and a towering statue of the Torchforger, Solovei. It is proud, short of people, and run on stubborn hope.

The people who live here come from every corner of the world, so cooking and tastes are varied. The Lightkeepers' oath ends with the line about shining the eternal light of hope into the endless snow-swept plains, and the city treats it as a working motto.

Geography: Piramida lies in Voidsea Outlook, at the southern end of the island of Pohjola, north of Paha Isle. It is built on a mountain around a giant lighthouse from the golden age, which in turn rests on the foundations of an older castle. Its highest level holds the great mead hall.

Places: The plaza with its bulletin board and officers, the Torchforger Statue, the Great Mead Hall, an infirmary with doctors, a blacksmith, and the central lighthouse. Illuga's house, where he cooks for guests, is also in the city.

People: Starshyna Nikita leads the Lightkeepers from here. Illuga, squad leader of the Nightmare Orioles and Nikita's adopted son, calls the city home. Ratniki in the plaza include Lyubertsi, Malusha, Marushkin (Sergeant Major) and Zimin, with Gabieta as Squad Leader; Ivar, Radoslaw and Lauri are in the infirmary, Hertta is the blacksmith, and Patolichev and Wszebor serve elsewhere in the city.

Governance: Piramida is the Lightkeepers' headquarters. The Starshyna leads, below him are Sergeant Majors, who coordinate Squad Leaders, who command Ratniki. Every Ratnik carries an Oath Lantern. Nod-Krai's autonomy under the Tsaritsa's old edict rests on the Lightkeepers, and the city defends it.

Culture: Duty and remembrance. Banquets after victories are for both celebration and mourning, graves are visited, and the oath is sworn by every Lightkeeper on joining. The Lightkeepers' symbol, a lighthouse on their flag and a nightingale with a burning wick, stands for keeping a beacon lit in the dark night.

History: The city sits on the foundations of the palace of Prokhor Trubetskoy, a fae Grand Duke who governed Nod-Krai before the Cataclysm. About 500 years ago the Torchforger, Solovei, won the Tsaritsa's leave to found the Lightkeepers and establish autonomy for Nod-Krai. Piramida became their base. In the 6.3 world quests the Lightkeepers launched the Arrow of Terpikeraunas from the mead hall and lighthouse to destroy the Abyssal Scourge of Endless Decay, which had lain sealed beneath Kipumaki Cliff since the Torchforger's day and which Nikita calls the undying fiend and the 'Professor'.

Dangers: The Wild Hunt is the constant threat, and patrol routes toward Dreadshade Mire and Afterglow Cavern have been hit. The Lightkeepers are understrength after years of losses; the Wildnight Owls squad was suspended after a failed operation.

Travel: Moonwagons, the Lightkeepers' kuuvahki-powered mobile lighthouses made from modified Snezhnayan vehicles, carry supplies between Piramida and the camps. The city lies in Voidsea Outlook on Pohjola.

Quests: The Nightingale's Song world quest series (6.3) runs through Piramida: Wind-Stirred Ripples, Tower of Inversion, When War Songs Rise and The Last Night, the First Light, the last of which sets the Arrow of Terpikeraunas and ends with a banquet. The Moonlit Watcher (II) has Illuga host the Traveler to dinner at his house.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Piramida is the Lightkeepers' working headquarters, still understrength but hopeful after destroying the Scourge in 6.3.

Nikita appears in the mead hall as Starshyna once the world quests conclude. The Abyssal crisis at Kipumaki Cliff is over, but the Wild Hunt remains and the Lightkeepers rebuild. Illuga says more people are asking to join and that even Nasha Town's merchants, normally indifferent to the public interest, are starting to see why the Lightkeepers fight. Nothing in 7.0-7.1 changes the city.

153.comment: Piramida: The Arrow of Terpikeraunas and the Mead Hall
153.content: Nikita explains that the Torchforger, five centuries ago, could only seal the undying fiend beneath Kipumaki Cliff, and so he and the first Moonchanter forged a bow and arrow to finish the job later. The mead hall was built to house it, and the Spiralblade recovered in the quests is its missing arrowhead. With the Spiralblade set in place, the lighthouse becomes a huge cannon, aimed at the Cataclysm Egg atop the Pillar of Embla.

154.content: Every Lightkeeper swears an oath on joining, which speaks of foreseeing a night sky devoured by silence, vowing to burn their bones and blood as fuel to make life greater than death, and ends with their promise to shine the light of hope into the snow-swept plains. Ratniki carry Oath Lanterns that let comrades and the Starshyna find them. The Starshyna is the leader, then Sergeant Majors, Squad Leaders and Ratniki.

155.content:
Pohjola: Pohjola is the large northern island of Nod-Krai, lying north of the Southern Isles. It is made up of Voidsea Outlook in the south, Wavechaser Plain and Ashveil Peak in the north and, by the wiki's grouping, Dunanna Pit. The Lightkeepers' city Piramida stands on it, and the frontier's abyssal and Wild Hunt dangers are felt here. Its name is borrowed from the cold northern land of Finnish mythology.

Voidsea Outlook, Wavechaser Plain and Ashveil Peak opened with Version 6.3 (Luna IV); Dunanna Pit came in 6.7. The old Hymns of the Far North place a passage into the Shadow Realm on Pohjola, but that book is an unreliable source.

Geography: Voidsea Outlook lies at the southern end of the island, just north of Paha Isle in the Southern Isles, and holds Piramida and Dreadshade Mire. Wavechaser Plain lies to its north and contains Lake Amsvartnir, Favonius Keep and the Pillar of Embla. Ashveil Peak is the northernmost part of the island and includes Kipumaki Cliff. Dunanna Pit is listed with Pohjola but is described elsewhere as east of it and close to Fontaine.

Places: Piramida, the Lightkeepers' headquarters, is a city built around a giant golden-age lighthouse, itself raised on the ruins of an older castle. North of it, Lake Amsvartnir hides the Royal Court of the Seelie. Favonius Keep in Wavechaser Plain is a Meeting Point; the Pillar of Embla also stands in this area. In Ashveil Peak, Lightkeeper allies appear and a boss called the Lord of the Hidden Depths: Whisperer of Nightmares is found.

History: Pohjola is named in the Hymns of the Far North. Its Prayer Song XVI says a young man named Saarelainen crossed the isle of Hiisi and the mist-shrouded lands of Pohjola to court Anastasya, and that the old man Pakkaisukko (the hymn's name for the Belyi Tsar) would grant her hand only if Saarelainen opened the gates of Pohjola, which the wiki links to the Shadow Realm. The prayer says a Lord of the Seven Calamities carved Saarelainen into seven pieces there.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Pohjola is open for travel and exploration, and the Lightkeepers hold it against the dark.

The island's Shadow Realm gate legend resurfaced in the 7.1 Archon Quest, but its truth is still contested by the sources.

156.content: Voidsea Outlook sits at Pohjola's southern end, north of Paha Isle, and contains Piramida, the Lightkeepers' headquarters city, and Dreadshade Mire. The Lightkeepers revere a statue of their founding Starshyna, Solovei the Torchforger. Piramida was built on the ruins of the castle of Prokhor Trubetskoy, around a golden-age lighthouse.

157.comment: Pohjola: Wavechaser Plain and Roland's Follower
157.content: Wavechaser Plain holds Favonius Keep, the Pillar of Embla and Lake Amsvartnir. Local specialties are Winter Icelea and Pine Amber, and Pale-Furred Wolves roam the plain. Lost Notes found here record a Mondstadt follower of the knight Roland.

158.content: The northernmost part of Pohjola, with Kipumaki Cliff. Wilderness Exiles, Wilderness Hunters and Fishers of Hidden Depths are common, Lightkeeper NPCs appear, and the Lord of the Hidden Depths: Whisperer of Nightmares is the area's boss.

159.content: Dunanna Pit opened in 6.7 (Luna VIII) and is close to Fontaine, east of Pohjola. It shares the Ancient Moon's Remnant at the Nuur Stone Circle with the Lunar Highlands rather than having its own Meeting Point. The name likely combines Sumerian roots for building and the moon god Nanna.

160.content: According to the Hymns of the Far North, Pohjola was where a passage into the Shadow Realm was opened by Anastasya and Saarelainen. In the prayer, the bride's father Pakkaisukko, the Belyi Tsar in the hymn, set opening the gates as the price of her hand, and Saarelainen went knowing the scheme. The book is unreliable, so its account is tradition, not fact.

161.content:
"Post-Apocalyptic Elysium" (also: Bunker No. 0): "Post-Apocalyptic Elysium" is a bunker in Wavechaser Plain, Nod-Krai, built in the reign of the Belyi Tsar to survive the supposed destruction of the world. Its researchers lived there believing the Abyss had devastated everything outside; their supervisor, Morozov, secretly served the plotter Rotwang.

The Traveler finds it in the world quest Return to Sender (6.3), restores its kuuvahki purification system and defeats the Abyssal monster that Morozov became. The bunker has a maintenance zone, a second-floor research zone and a third-floor supervisor's office.

History: The bunker held a team of researchers and their families under Supervisor R. M. Morozov. Senior Researcher Grazina Myklukho bred plants with an affinity for kuuvahki that absorbed it and purified Abyssal corruption, and Morozov approved pipes to circulate it through the ventilation as the "Apocalypse Purification System". But Morozov used the experiments to let Abyssal monsters loose in the experiment zones. Repeated breaches killed people, including a child, Payva, and Grazina's written protests were ignored. Maintenance Worker Kotelnikov learned that the outside world was intact and was silenced.

Places: A maintenance zone at the entrance; a second-floor research zone with two experiment sites, valves and a control terminal; a third-floor supervisory office. Readable logs, recordings and a private journal tell the story.

Dangers: Rifthounds and, on the third floor, the Ultimate Calamity that Morozov became; Abyssal corruption.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the bunker is open and its monster destroyed. Grazina's fate is recorded as sealing herself inside about 500 years ago.

162.content:
Reed Miller's Great Treasure (also: The Great Treasure, The Final Treasure Site, Elysium's Final Treasure): Reed Miller's Great Treasure is a hidden cave beneath Dreadshade Mire in Nod-Krai, holding a huge pile of Iron Coins heaped on a ship. In folklore it is the great hoard of Reed Miller, the Treasure Hoarders' legendary master thief. In truth it was arranged about 500 years ago by Brahe, the third man to use that alias, as part of a plan to bury the real Reed Miller under harmless tall tales. The Traveler finds it by collecting the five Proofs of the Cognoscenti.

Entry is through the world quest The Raven's Legacy, the final part of East of the Moon, West of the Sun. The vault is a trial: three locked doors, riddling notices, a Weasel Thief statue and a guardian monster. Inside, the ship's helm triggers a vision of two thieves in the past, and Brahe's Notes explain the whole scheme.

Geography: Beneath Dreadshade Mire in the Voidsea Outlook area, reached through a hole opened under a giant Weasel Thief statue. The map shows three levels: the Entrance, an Entrance Hall and the Destination, where the ship and its Iron Coins lie.

Places: The Weasel Thief statue with five Iron Coins hanging from its tail, which the Traveler feeds the five Proofs of the Cognoscenti; the three doors; a stone tablet with a verse about a raven felled in a net amid thorn-bushes; and the ship under its mound of Iron Coins.

People: Brahe is the author of the vault and of Brahe's Notes. Tolfin, the storyteller who guides the quest, and his grandmother Hiljetta (who fights the Traveler as a friendly spar) lead the way to it. Two thieves named Relya and Silve appear in the helm flashback.

History: Brahe, last Governor of Nod-Krai after the Cataclysm, saw his friends Avrelian and Alia gone and their ideals twisted by bandits who used the name Reed Miller to justify cruelty. He decided to smother their history under contradictory legends. He placed a vault of Iron Coins, with the help of wild weasels, to give the name a harmless, absurd legend of a Great Treasure and keep the tales alive for future Treasure Hoarders.

Culture: The Treasure Hoarders revere the legend of Reed Miller, and the Great Treasure is its crowning tale. Popular versions appear in The Legends of Reed Miller, Thief Extraordinaire. Tolfin estimates 20 percent of the legend comes from Alia, 30 percent from Brahe, and the rest is invention.

Atmosphere: A theatrical puzzle-cave: riddling notices, scurrying weasels, coin-strewn passages and a playful but sober closing message. The flashback at the helm is solemn.

Dangers: A Radiant Lunapod, Guard of Lost Treasures, attacks when the chest is opened. The doors can also be solved without combat.

Travel: Begin The Raven's Legacy in Piramida with Tolfin, spar with Hiljetta, and bring the five Proofs of the Cognoscenti to the statue. Afterwards a teleport waypoint marks the entrance.

Quests: The Raven's Legacy (World Quest, final part of East of the Moon, West of the Sun): after Tolfin points the Traveler and Paimon to the vault, they solve the door puzzles, find the strange Iron Coins, defeat the guardian, and take the ship's helm. The flashback shows Relya and Silve, two thieves of the past, taking treasure from a governor and leaving a raven insignia in its place. The Traveler receives The First Iron Coin.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the vault is open to explore. The hoard of Iron Coins is still on the ship, and nothing after 7.1 is recorded.

163.comment: Reed Miller's Great Treasure: Reed Miller
163.content: In Nod-Krai folklore Reed Miller is the founder of the Treasure Hoarders and a master thief, but the name was an alias used by at least three people: Avrelian, Alia and Brahe. Brahe deliberately seeded contradictory legends, including the Great Treasure, so that those who might misuse the name would not be taken seriously.

164.comment: Reed Miller's Great Treasure: Brahe's Notes
164.content: Brahe's Notes are four writings found in the vault in which Brahe explains how he arranged the Iron Coins with the help of Weasel Thieves, how Avrelian and Silvestr once took his father's hidden funds, and why he felt compelled to cover Avrelian and Alia's legacy in harmless legends. He saw goodwill as wasted on poisoned soil, in a thought he attributes to Alia's gloomy sister Aila.

165.content:
Rossum Workshop: The Rossum Workshop is a smithy in Nasha Town, Nod-Krai. The blacksmith Arkhyp owns it, and his daughter Lyulka currently runs it.

Lyulka is the vendor, listed as a researcher; Arkhyp is named as the workshop's blacksmith.

People: Arkhyp, the blacksmith and owner. Lyulka, his daughter, who operates the workshop at present and has her own entry.

Status as of 7.1: Operating as of 7.1; no change recorded.

166.content:
Royal Court of the Seelie (also: Royal Court of the Seelies, Palaces of Times Bygone, pale temple of Koitar): The Royal Court of the Seelie is a pale temple hidden above Lake Amsvartnir in Nod-Krai, invisible to ordinary eyes. Legend and ancient notes place the first Seelie, Koitar, wife of Anacharsis, here after the Heavenly Principles wiped her memory. The Traveler and the Seelie of the lake break its barrier and restore it in the world quest Echoes of a Forsaken Song.

Reaching it means melting a Lunar Conflux Barrier at the lake, playing a lyre that only the player seems to hear, and riding Moonlanes up through floating islands while reconnecting Lakeside Prisms. Each prism brings back a verse of an old lament, and three Ancient Handwriting notes in the court hold Koitar's own words.

Geography: The court sits above the lake of Amsvartnir, north of Piramida in Wavechaser Plain, beyond the ruins of an ancient palace on the edge of the wasteland. Its approach is a sacred forest by the water. The old description says it cannot be seen by mortals in daylight, and that whoever breaks the golden branch in the forest will find it.

History: Canon casts the court as a place of confinement. After the failed Hyperborean rebellion against the Heavenly Principles, Koitar lost her memories and was held in a temple that, in her own account, she could not leave and no passer-by could see. Her tiny kin, the Seelie, mourned beside her though she no longer knew them. Thousands of years later, the Traveler follows the Seelie to Amsvartnir and uncovers it.

People: No one lives here now. Koitar, the first Seelie, is the court's only named occupant, and the Seelie of the lake are its guides; both belong to the past of the place. See the character entry for Koitar for her wider story.

Dangers: Nothing hostile is tied to the court itself. The lake area has its own wildlife and enemies, such as pale-furred wolves and a radiant glacial wolf, and the court is reached by puzzle rather than by combat.

Quests: The only quest is the world quest Echoes of a Forsaken Song (6.3, Wavechaser Plain). Its rewards include chests and the Ancient Handwriting notes, and it grants the achievement Farewell Hope, With Hope Farewell Fear.

Status as of 7.1: Revealed and restored, and open to explore as of 7.1. No later story has revisited it.

167.comment: Royal Court of the Seelie: Koitar's Lament (Ancient Handwriting)
167.content: Three readable notes in the court preserve Koitar's thoughts after her memory was cut away. The first describes the temple, her emptiness, the voice that bids her wait, and her decision to sing. The second tells of the wolf she named Boreas. The third is addressed to Anacharsis and, bitterly, to the Heavenly Principles; she resolves to go back to Hyperborea and wait for him.

168.comment: Royal Court of the Seelie: Echoes of a Forsaken Song
168.content: This world quest begins by playing the lyre at Amsvartnir after melting a Lunar Conflux Barrier. The Traveler follows a Seelie up Moonlanes, reconnects Lakeside Prisms to release verses, breaks seals on four floating islands, and restores the court and its mural, ending with chests and the Ancient Handwriting notes.

169.content:
Sanctum of Departed Heroes (also: Hall of Resounding Valor): The Sanctum of Departed Heroes is the final resting place of many Lightkeepers who died in battle, at Kipumaki Cliff in Ashveil Peak, Nod-Krai. It was once a hotspot of Wild Hunt activity. Its viewpoint is named the Hall of Resounding Valor.

Two diary entries by a newly selected Lightkeeper recruit are kept here, continuing one found at the Pillar of Embla.

Geography: In Ashveil Peak, at Kipumaki Cliff, close to Cliffwatch Camp and the Chasm of Endless Decay. An unsigned diary calls Kipumaki Cliff itself the place "often called" the Sanctum of Departed Heroes, the resting ground of soldiers who fell in battle.

History: Piramida ordered a support unit stationed at Kipumaki Cliff to clear Wild Hunt nests; the Frostgale Steeds were called in as reinforcements during a sudden outbreak that spilled onto the ramparts of the Sanctum. Lightkeepers who died in such fights are laid to rest here.

People: The three diary entries in this set belong to the recruit Filaev, under Captain Asebov in a support unit with Chernov, Shonokovych and Patolichev. The second entry describes the terror of his first mission: he froze as a monster threw itself at him and was saved by Chernov, and afterwards wondered whether he would die or see his mother and Nasha Town again.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Sanctum is open to exploration; the wiki describes it as having once been a Wild Hunt hotspot.

170.comment: Sanctum of Departed Heroes: Filaev's Diary
170.content: Filaev passed the Ratnik selection with the lowest rank, loved the uniform and the lantern with his name on it, and hoped his story would reach Nasha Town. Posted to a support unit at Kipumaki Cliff, he spent months in routine until Piramida ordered the unit to clear Wild Hunt nests, which he took as his first chance to prove himself. His fate is not recorded.

171.content:
Sanctum of the Oathbearer (also: Court of the First Edict, Lies of the Faithless): The Sanctum of the Oathbearer, also called the Court of the First Edict, is a sealed ceremonial sanctum of the Frostmoon Scions on Hiisi Island. Until five hundred years ago the Scions held their rites here. After Aila learned of Lovia's treachery and killed her, she sealed the order's ancient documents and the evidence of Lovia's corruption inside, to stop any later leader from rising as Lovia did. It is reopened in the world quest Echoes of an Unfinished Past.

The loading screen describes it as a sealed sacred sanctum, and says that the dark places moonlight cannot touch do not hide only blessings. It is entered from the base of the Sanctum of the Oathkeeper.

Geography: Entered from the base of the Sanctum of the Oathkeeper. The interactable documents are on the upper level; the ground level holds the White Spring, where Aila left the ritual sword Moonweaver's Dawn. A Moonlane leads through the Court during the quest.

History: Aila sealed the Court after assassinating Lovia, the Archpriestess whose rule had corrupted the Frostmoon Scions. She stored the order's ancient documents and proof of Lovia's corruption here, and left Moonweaver's Dawn, a ritual sword forged by Anacharsis in the Hyperborean era, in the White Spring. The place stayed sealed until Verna and the Traveler opened it in Echoes of an Unfinished Past, as Aila had predicted.

Quests: Echoes of an Unfinished Past (a world quest of the chapter Polkka Beneath the Moon's Oracle) starts at the Light-Bathed Platform: Verna asks the Traveler to throw fragments to open the sanctum, follow the Moonlane, unlock a mechanism seal, enter the Court, and investigate the sword Aila left behind. Completing it earns the achievement The Weaver in the Ossuary.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Sanctum of the Oathbearer is unsealed and open to exploration.

172.comment: Sanctum of the Oathbearer: Aila's Notes
172.content: Aila's private notes record that she lied, as Lovia and her sister Alia had, when Solovei asked whether she felt hatred, because she did not want to burden him. She calls her hatred horrifying and does not want it understood. She resolves that everything of the old order must be torn down but the sanctuary, that kindness to outlanders and reverence for nature should set the Scions apart, and that the Frostmoon Scions must leave the future new moon goddess free to choose. She foresees a new moon goddess born decades later, that Lovia's long quest was for nothing, and that the Scions, redeemed in her name, must never demand repayment from her.

173.comment: Sanctum of the Oathbearer: Letters to Lovia and Aila
173.content: The Letter for Lovia is signed by Rotwang. It reports that the "holy lady" his agents were told to bring to Lovia killed herself on the spot, offers sympathy and gifts, and agrees that they must find another way to rouse the Sampo Mill and build an "Elysium" for the people of Nod-Krai. The Letter for Aila is signed by Solovei. He laments that he could not stop Alia, thanks her for her sacrifice against Rotwang, passes on her last wish that Aila live a life of happiness and freedom, and agrees to receive the Arrow of Terpikeraunas, proposing to call his successors the Lightkeepers.

174.comment: Sanctum of the Oathbearer: Moonweaver's Dawn and the White Spring
174.content: Moonweaver's Dawn is a ritual sword forged by Anacharsis in the Hyperborean era. Aila placed it in the White Spring at the Court's ground level. At the end of Echoes of an Unfinished Past the Traveler investigates the sword she left behind.

175.comment: Sanctum of the Oathbearer: The Verdant Crest
175.content: The Verdant Crest is a divine tree in the middle of the Court, said to have appeared alongside the Moon Maiden Columbina. In the book Hymns of the Far North, an annotator points out that it also appears in hymns of rituals older than the Moon Maiden's birth five centuries ago, which should not be possible.

176.content:
Sanctum of the Oathkeeper: The Sanctum of the Oathkeeper is an exterior area on Hiisi Island in Nod-Krai. It provides access to two instanced locations: the Sanctum of the Oathbearer and the Interstice of the Nearing Moon.

The Sanctum of the Oathbearer (Court of the First Edict) is entered from its base after being unsealed in Echoes of an Unfinished Past.

Geography: Exterior grounds on Hiisi Island serving as the doorway to the two instances. The wiki gives no further description of its layout.

History: No history for the Oathkeeper site itself is stated in the sources read. The inner Sanctum of the Oathbearer was sealed by Aila five hundred years ago.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the area is open and serves as the entrance to the Oathbearer and the Interstice.

key: Knights of Favonius meeting place in Nod-Krai
177.content:
Secret Base (also: "Secret Base", the secret base, Knights of Favonius meeting place in Nod-Krai): The Secret Base is a well-hidden underground meeting place on Lempo Isle in Nod-Krai. Grand Master Varka describes it as the Knights of Favonius's meeting place in Nod-Krai and a contact hub for the Northern Intelligence Network, the continent's black market of information. Only story quests open its interior: the allies of Song of the Welkin Moon gather there to plan against the Wild Hunt and its master, Rerir.

Varka brings the party there after rescuing them from a Wild Hunt ambush in Hidden in the Shadows. Nefer, the Network's representative, turns up there because a letter from a 'humble knight of Favonius' asked her to a meeting about a business deal; she knows where it is because she runs the arrangement. The base later hosts several visitors, including Arlecchino, Albedo, Durin and Dainsleif.

Geography: Underground on Lempo Isle, somewhere reached through the open world but not enterable outside quests. The interior is a hidden gathering space where the group sits and talks; Varka says it is secure, and Paimon remarks how well hidden it is.

People: Varka, Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, uses it as his meeting place. In Hidden in the Shadows Aino, Ineffa, Flins, Jahoda, Lauma, Columbina (as the Damselette), Paimon and the Traveler gather there against the Wild Hunt; later scenes feature Varka, Jahoda, Lauma and others returning from their missions. Nefer, who runs the Northern Intelligence Network, knows of it and is paid for helping. Later visitors are the Fourth Harbinger Arlecchino, Albedo, Durin and Dainsleif.

History: Introduced in version 6.1 with Song of the Welkin Moon Act III. The wiki gives no origin for the place beyond Varka's description. The Knights' expedition had been working in Nod-Krai well before the Traveler arrived, and Varka says the Network has been its best source of local intelligence.

Quests: Hidden in the Shadows (Archon Quest, Act III, part 1): after being surrounded by the Wild Hunt, the Traveler's party is led by Varka to the secret base, where Nefer unexpectedly arrives, agrees to help Jahoda for this once, and Varka lays out three priorities: a way to beat Rerir, finding out his end goal, and stalling him while the others act; the group splits into three teams. Everlasting As the Moon (part 3): the party returns to share findings and meets Arlecchino. All Is Foretold (Act IV, part 1): Albedo and Durin, and then Dainsleif, join the planning.

Atmosphere: A secure room for conspiring: friendly banter, hard strategy, and a mood that tightens with each new arrival. In All Is Foretold the room fills so much that Varka jokes about running out of chairs and Albedo offers to make more.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the base remains the Knights' hidden meeting place in Nod-Krai and is enterable only in the three quests above. Nothing newer is recorded.

178.content: The Northern Intelligence Network is an underground information market run by Nefer from the Curatorium of Secrets in Nod-Krai, with contacts in every nation. Varka calls it the black market of intel; the Knights use it because it is reliable. Members and informants include Jahoda, Sarin and Diluc, and clients include Varka.

179.content: Varka holds war councils at the secret base, deciding how to defeat Rerir and the Wild Hunt. He tells the party that the Knights, as an expeditionary force, need the Network to learn what is happening locally.

180.content:
Silvermoon Hall (also: Moon-Bathed Courtyard, Silvermoon Courtyard): Silvermoon Hall is a moon-themed cavern on Hiisi Island in Nod-Krai, the hiding place of Columbina after she left the Fatui. The player first enters it during Reunion Beneath the Moonlight, in the Archon Quest chapter Song of the Welkin Moon. While inside, only the Traveler can be controlled and Co-Op Mode is disabled.

The map description reads: the new moon always listens to the wishes of the living, laughter or tears, joy or sorrow; one wonders whether the new moon has a wish of its own.

Geography: A cavern on Hiisi Island whose viewpoint is the Moon-Bathed Courtyard. The local specialty is Moonfall Silver. Columbina and the Record-Keeping Kuuhenki are the resident NPCs.

History: Silvermoon Hall appears in the Archon Quest after Columbina leaves the Fatui; it becomes the place the Traveler visits to meet her. Its reputation system, Silvermoon Hall: Selenic Chronicles, is unlocked by completing The Dark Side of Memory.

People: Columbina is hiding here. The Record-Keeping Kuuhenki lets the player view the Selenic Chronicles records.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Hall remains Columbina's hiding place and is visited through the Selenic Chronicles quests.

181.content:
Skymount: Skymount is a huge elevator that connects Ungien's Circle, the Frost Moon's biosphere, to the Space Lifeform Capture Station in space above it.

It opens in the world quest Visitors From the Stars, during which the Traveler rides it up to the station. Afterwards it can be used in both directions, and a cutscene plays on each ride.

Geography: It rises from Ungien's Circle to the station, which hangs in space over the biosphere. Once at the station, travellers enter a weightless state and only the Traveler (plus Columbina if owned) can take part.

Travel: Canon describes it as the link between the biosphere and the station; the ride is brief and plays as a cutscene.

Status as of 7.1: Working as of 7.1.

182.content:
South Harbor: The South Harbor is a harbor of the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau on Paha Isle, Nod-Krai. A notice at the North Harbor routes all goods entering the Bureau through it.

Seafarers are found here, and a board carries stern notices about the Bureau's equipment.

People: Listed NPCs: Azalea, Przybor (crew member of the Ocean Dawn), Risto, Tuokko (captain of the Never Fade Away) and Veroslava.

Status as of 7.1: In use as of 7.1; it carries the Bureau's freight while the North Harbor stays closed.

183.content:
Southern Isles (also: Lempo Isles, Three Southern Isles): The Southern Isles, also called the Lempo Isles, are a group of three islands at the south of Nod-Krai, lying south of Pohjola: Lempo Isle, Hiisi Island and Paha Isle. Together with the city of Piramida they are the most populated part of Nod-Krai. Lempo Isle holds Nasha Town and the inventors' workshops, Hiisi Island is the wild home of the Frostmoon Scions, and Paha Isle is the Fatui's staging ground.

The islands became explorable with Version 6.0 (Luna I, 2025-09-10) and are the region's most populated area alongside Piramida. They are named with Finnic mythological words: Lempo, Hiisi and Paha are all figures or terms from the Kalevala tradition.

Geography: Lempo Isle is the central island of the group, with Nasha Town, the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop and the highland plateaus of Barrowmoss Barrens around Blue Amber Lake. Hiisi Island is mostly untouched forest wilderness. Paha Isle, once known for sunset-coloured salt marshes and colonies of Tassel Jellies, now hosts the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau.

Places: Lempo Isle: Nasha Town (home of the Speranza restaurant), the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop run by Aino, Barrowmoss Barrens and Blue Amber Lake. Hiisi Island: the Light-Bathed Platform and the forest sanctuaries of the Frostmoon Scions. Paha Isle: the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau.

People: Lempo Isle is the home of ordinary Nod-Krai townsfolk and inventors, including Aino, whose craftshop is based there. Hiisi Island belongs to the Frostmoon Scions, a religious sect devoted to the Goddess of the New Moon, and the Fatui personnel of Nod-Krai use Paha Isle as a staging ground.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the islands are open and inhabited. Hiisi Island's moon cult and Paha Isle's Fatui bureau are the two forces that most affect events.

Columbina was reported near Hiisi Island in 6.0; consult her entry for later developments.

184.comment: Southern Isles: Lempo Isle and Nasha Town
184.content: Lempo Isle is the main settled island, including Nasha Town (with the Speranza restaurant), Aino's Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop, and Barrowmoss Barrens with Blue Amber Lake. The wiki notes Frostlamp Flower and Portable Bearing as local specialties and Knuckle Duckle as a boss. Amazing 'Bots roam the island.

185.content: A forested island that is the home of the Frostmoon Scions, a sect devoted to the Goddess of the New Moon. Much of it is untouched wilderness. The Light-Bathed Platform and the Frostnight Herra are found here, and Moonfall Silver and Frostlamp Flower can be gathered.

186.comment: Southern Isles: Paha Isle and the Kuuvahki Bureau
186.content: Paha Isle is the Fatui's staging ground in Nod-Krai. Its Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau is a high-tech complex. The island's earlier fame came from salt marshes and Tassel Jellies, until the heaviest moonstone fragment fell on it. Paha is a word for bad or evil in Finnic languages and, in the Kalevala, a demon follower of Lempo.

187.content:
Space Lifeform Capture Station (also: Capture Station, Skymount destination): The Space Lifeform Capture Station is a dragon-built space station floating above Ungien's Circle on the Frost Moon. The researcher Ungien made it to capture or contact the alien creatures he believed lived among the stars, so as to prove his belief that the deep-space signal came from such a being. A huge elevator called the Skymount carries visitors up from the moon to reach it.

It forms the upper half of a single complex with the Ungien Biosphere below. The Traveler, Paimon and Eggie rode up in the first Visitors From the Stars quest and found Columbina floating at a window inside, watching Maggie, the Mega Kuuhenki.

Geography: The station is in space proper, far enough above the moon that the party sees Teyvat from it. Inside, everything is weightless; the party is limited to the Traveler plus Columbina if owned. Rooms: the Main Observation Room, the Gravity Control Room, the Space Capture Arm and, outside, the wrecked Moongazer.

Places: Main Observation Room (a view of Teyvat and a model of the three moons). Gravity Control Room (a Gravimeter). Space Capture Arm (presumed capture corridor, damaged). Moongazer Wreckage (see location.moongazer).

People: Ungien, life scientist, designer; Maagees-Geti, his partner, who investigated the Moongazer and later became the Mega Kuuhenki Maggie; Lusalim, their student. In the story only Columbina, Maggie and the Traveler's party are present.

History: Ungien built the station as part of Project Moongazer to prove his theory that the deep-space signal received by the dragon pioneers came from an alien lifeform, not from the dragon king as Ibni-Belum had held. His own voyage in the Moongazer ended when the ship returned cloaked years later and struck the station's Space Capture Arm.

Dangers: Inside, nothing hostile is shown; the risks are the lift (the Skymount fails when power is out), weightlessness, and the energy storms that rise from the lunar sea below.

Travel: Reached by the Skymount elevator inside the great tree of Ungien's Circle. The lift needed the Ungien power engine repaired, which the party did by clearing Knotted Moonlight Vines from its turbines and escaping before they restarted.

Quests: Visitors From the Stars (Part 1 and Part 2), Moon Gazing chapter Act II (6.7). The hidden exploration quest A Journey's End also starts at the Space Capture Arm.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the station is damaged but intact and open to visitors via the Skymount.

Columbina treats it as part of her home to be tidied. Ungie and Maggie, the two Mega Kuuhenki, live in the lunar sea below, not in the station.

188.comment: Space Lifeform Capture Station: Skymount and Ungien's Circle Power Engine
188.content: The Skymount is a huge lift set against the great tree of Ungien's Circle. It failed at first for lack of energy. A blueprint terminal showed that the complex has two parts, the Ungien Biosphere on the ground and the capture station in orbit, and that its power hub sits underground fed by a sea of dense ancient-moon energy beneath Ungien's Circle. The party restored four turbines to reboot it.

key: Dottore's lab in the far north
189.content:
Special Territory Research Institute (also: Dottore's lab in the far north): The Special Territory Research Institute is a Fatui research facility on Ashveil Peak, in the far north of Nod-Krai. It is Dottore's base during Song of the Welkin Moon, and secrets lie deep beneath its foundations. After the story it becomes the False Moon Institute, a domain where players can replay the fight with the Heretic of the False Moon.

Ashveil Peak is part of Pohjola, the northernmost part of that island. In the domain's text, the facility "stands upon the northern reaches of Nod-Krai" and conceals secrets "as deep and uncharted as the structures buried far beneath its foundations." The same text says that at dusk memories of a battle that tore the sky apart linger, and that the moon has at last returned home.

Geography: It lies on Ashveil Peak, the northernmost part of Pohjola, in the far north of Nod-Krai, north of Voidsea Outlook and Paha Isle where the Fatui's Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau stands. The wiki lists it as a subarea of Ashveil Peak, and the only listed feature is the False Moon Institute domain.

People: Dottore, the Fatui Harbinger known as the Doctor, treats it as his lair. A Fatui soldier named Jotautas is found inside; he had served in the unit assigned to Columbina in Nod-Krai, then came under Dottore's command when she left the Fatui. Sandrone and Arlecchino, also Harbingers, go to the facility before the Traveler's party.

History: After Columbina banished herself into the moon's reflection and Dottore lost control of the powers of the Three Moons that he had gained on Moon-Prayer Night, the wiki's account says he retreated to this facility. He later made an artificial Moon Marrow to replace Columbina's, and the Traveler's group returns to confront him there in Act VII of Song of the Welkin Moon.

Dangers: Fatui soldiers, Landcruisers and monsters in the approach; Dottore's own traps and spaces. In domain form, the Heretic of the False Moon is a weekly boss whose rewards include the Mask of the Virtuous Doctor, Madman's Restraint and Elixir of the Heretic, with recommended levels of 60 to 90.

Quests: Act VII, A Traveler on a Winter's Night (Version 6.3), has the party fighting Dottore here. The domain False Moon Institute unlocks after completing Welkin Moon's Homecoming.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Institute is a replayable domain, and the story treats the moon as returned to its place in the sky.

190.comment: Special Territory Research Institute: Dottore's Artificial Moon Marrow
190.content: Dottore made an artificial Moon Marrow to substitute for Columbina after she banished herself from his control, and with it he could simply restore his injuries during the fight at the facility. The wiki says he then used his artificial moon to replace the Frost Moon in the sky, which Arlecchino explains to the group. Jotautas, a former subordinate of Columbina, says her old unit learned that Dottore was trying to make an artificial Moon Marrow.

191.comment: Special Territory Research Institute: False Moon Institute Domain
191.content: A trounce domain on Ashveil Peak, unlocked after Welkin Moon's Homecoming, in which players relive the battle with the Heretic of the False Moon. It is a gameplay replay and uses the memories of the fight, not a new event.

192.content:
Speranza (also: Speranza restaurant, Katya's eatery): Speranza is the reasonably priced restaurant that retired bounty hunter Katya runs in Nasha Town, Nod-Krai. It is the main eatery of the region, popular with ordinary residents and treasure hunters, and the Conch Gang, the young staff and strays Katya looks after, treat it as their home base.

The in-game map text calls it Katya's reasonably priced eatery and the Conch Gang's unofficial headquarters when they are not helping out. Speranza is also one of the powers with influence over Nasha Town, which has no official governing body: the others the wiki names are the Voynich Guild, the Curatorium of Secrets and the Fatui. The name means "hope" in Italian.

People: Katya is a former adventurer of the Treasure Hoarders who retired after injuries. She takes in children who end up on the street, gives them jobs, food and housing, and lets them live as freely as they like. Staff include Jurva, called the super chef, and the hosts Maisie and Mikko. Other regulars are Bedriskaya and Borzyslaw, and the dog Pavlov. Three Knights of Favonius, Arved, Helmut and Silja, are listed among its NPCs.

Places: A restaurant in Nasha Town, marked on the map with a restaurant icon. Katya sells food, recipes and ingredients: Nod-Krai Hot Dog, Lakkaberry Madame, Midsommar Torte and Crispy Roast daily, plus weekly basics such as flour, cream and sausage. After the Archon Quest Rest Beyond Reach, the shop gives a permanent 10 percent discount.

History: Per one story told by Jurva, a group of children once "conquered" Nasha Town by blowing a conch to call gatherings, which is how the gang got its name; the town later grew into a bustling settlement and the gang no longer dominated it. In Aino's character story, the Snezhnayan mechanic Papa Wrench ate at Speranza, saw the children, and with Katya's approval taught a small class on machines in the restaurant's downtime, which is how Aino began her training.

Quests: After the world quest Priorities First (Version 6.0), a white Weasel Thief that stole Paimon's Mora is found outside Speranza, surrounded by Maisie, Mikko and Jurva, who pin it down; the Mora is returned, and the children discuss what to do with it later with Katya.

Atmosphere: Warm and busy, with hot food, young staff and a fortune wheel and a food-hunting dog outside. Katya keeps an eye on the children and is firm about not letting them be endangered.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Speranza is open, still run by Katya, and still the Conch Gang's base.

193.content: The Conch Gang is the group of stray children under Katya's care. Members include Auni, Semyon, Helka, Jurva, Maisie, Maite and Mikko; former members include Aino, Linnea and Tapani. A new member needs the agreement of all existing members, and the gang traditionally accepts children and asks members to leave at a certain age, though there is precedent for admitting an older person. Maite calls the Traveler an official friend of the gang during The Mirrors, the Maze, and the Tsar.

194.content: Katya is the owner of Speranza, a former Treasure Hoarders adventurer who retired after injuries. She welcomes visitors, sells food, jokes that the kids are happy to work for their share, and tells people to look elsewhere for treasure rumors. After The Mirrors, the Maze, and the Tsar, once only, she gives the Traveler Nod-Krai Hot Dogs and Fonta because of Maite's message.

195.comment: Speranza: Pavlov and the Lucky Spin
195.content: Pavlov is a dog at Speranza who asks guests to spin a wheel because, once it has been spun and stopped, good food falls. He is understood by people who can hear animals, such as Lauma and Columbina. Passers-by are allowed to spin the wheel too, but a notice reminds visitors that everything belongs to Speranza and Pavlov is watching.

196.content:
Starsand Shoal: Starsand Shoal is the western beach of Lempo Isle in Nod-Krai. The wiki records it as the place where the spaceship of the Traveler and their sibling landed. Its expedition description says that when a dark disaster engulfed Nod-Krai many heroes made their last stand on these sands, and that the whispering waves still sing of their valor.

It lies in the Southern Isles on the island's west coast. Stones placed by the Lightkeepers, the Tideseal Stones, stand to its north and south to dispel the permeation of the Wild Hunt, and Wild Hunt pockets lie close by.

Geography: Open sand and shallows on Lempo Isle's western edge, with a Teleport Waypoint near the middle. Tideseal Stones stand north and south of it, each with a Wild Hunt area.

History: The in-game description ties the shoal to an unspecified past disaster: heroes made their final stand here when darkness overran Nod-Krai. The wiki records a later arrival: the Traveler's and their sibling's spaceship came down on this shore.

People: Semyon, a child near the waypoint, hopes to publish a report on the Fatui. Alice, as seen in A Mother's Last Wish, arranges a meeting with Durin on the shoal.

Quests: Crimes Against Jelly-kind (hidden objective, unofficial name; rewards Semyon's Notes and the Ice Cream Cutie blueprint), The Bell of Mourning Echoes and Secrets of the Tideseal Stones (Tideseal Stones nearby), and the start of A Mother's Last Wish (6.2).

Dangers: Wild Hunt creatures patrol the areas by the Tideseal Stones; Radiant Beasts appear in A Mother's Last Wish.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it remains an open beach on Lempo Isle's west coast, with Lightkeeper stones holding the Wild Hunt at bay.

Nothing in the pages read marks any change to the shoal after 6.2.

197.content:
Thunderclap Reef: Thunderclap Reef is a rocky reef in the southwest of Hiisi Island, Nod-Krai. Its kuuvahki has been unstable since at least 500 years ago, giving it a strong kuuvahki environment, and the Frostmoon Scions treat it as a forbidden place. Two large Moon Fragments fell there recently and made things worse.

In the world quest For a Green Island..., the Traveler and Paimon help the self-styled priestess Verna remove the fragments and partly stabilise the kuuvahki. Afterwards the weather there is perpetually rainy.

Geography: A rocky reef on the southwest of Hiisi Island, with caves, a high summit and a Moon Mirror at the top. Before the quest the area is a red strong kuuvahki environment.

People: Verna, a young woman in Frostmoon robes who calls herself a priestess and the finest mechanic on Hiisi Island, works here with small helper robots named Kraka (models III, V and VII appear). She says she is a direct apprentice of the mechanic known as Papa Wrench.

History: Verna says the kuuvahki at the reef has been unstable since the time of the first Moonchanter, Lady Aila, and that the trouble grew worse after two large rocks fell from the sky.

Dangers: Strong, unstable kuuvahki, and (during the quest) lightning storms. Cave collapses also occur; one blocks the original exit while the Traveler and Paimon search for fragments.

Quests: For a Green Island... (world quest, chapter Polkka Beneath the Moon's Oracle): begins automatically when approaching the reef. The wiki also lists Animal Research: Chic Badgers and Everlasting As the Moon as touching the area; they are not summarised here.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the reef's kuuvahki is partly stabilised but still strong, and rain is constant.

198.comment: Thunderclap Reef: For a Green Island...
198.content: In this world quest Verna recruits the Traveler and Paimon to calm the reef by throwing fragments at two boulders. The plan briefly makes the kuuvahki worse; then a robed woman holding the final fragment at the Moon Mirror lets them have it, cryptically speaking of a newborn "god" and saying she will await them at the Court of the First Edict. The kuuvahki is afterwards somewhat steadier and the weather turns rainy.

199.content:
Traveler's Crater (also: Wayfarer's Crater): Traveler's Crater is the huge crater on the Frost Moon in whose centre the Traveler's spaceship rests. Columbina led the Traveler here in Welkin Moon's Homecoming (6.3), when it was a quest-only location, and from the Moon Gazing quests (6.7) it can be visited freely. Teyvat hangs in the sky above it.

The viewpoint here is called The Next Journey. The crater can be reached by the High-Speed Transit Lane from the Nuur Stone Circle.

Geography: A wide lunar crater under low gravity, with the star-shaped, white-and-gold spaceship standing at its centre. Columbina first reached it on foot across the lunar plain, after crossing a path of moonlight and a boat on a lake of Moon-Prayer Blossoms from Teyvat.

Atmosphere: Open lunar ground under a sky where the world of Teyvat is visible. Columbina remarks that she could spend a whole day looking at Teyvat from here, and that she took off her eye mask to see it.

History: The Heavenly Principles hid the spaceship on the Frost Moon after the Cataclysm. Columbina sensed it after she became the Trilune Goddess and took the Traveler there. The Traveler read the logs aboard, collected an old outfit, and learned that the ship had flown over Teyvat once, much earlier, without landing. See the spaceship entry for details.

Quests: Visited during Welkin Moon's Homecoming (6.3), then made permanently available in the Moon Gazing quests. A post-quest conversation with Columbina here follows Project Moongazer (Part 2).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the crater is open and the spaceship remains where the Heavenly Principles placed it.

200.content:
Underground Energy Generation Station: The Underground Energy Generation Station is one of three stations that generate energy for the Eye of Ibni-Belum on the Frost Moon. It makes Ancient Moon Pearls, spheres that store and transport Archaeolune Energy.

After Pioneers (Part 2), its terminal shows a dedication to Ibni-Belum, the pioneer who went ahead of everyone, "the first Moongazer", for his contributions to Project Moongazer.

Geography: It lies below the ground in the Eye of Ibni-Belum area. The Ancient Moon Pearls can be rolled around and pushed into power stations, which then pass the energy along Archaeolune Energy Pathways to run machinery.

History: The station is part of the power supply of the Eye of Ibni-Belum, the facility from which the Moongazers' message is later sent into space. Beyond the terminal dedication, canon gives no building date or builder for this station.

Status as of 7.1: Ancient and explorable as of 7.1.

201.content:
Underground Research Center (also: Secret Research): The Underground Research Center is a classified Fatui research site below the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau on Paha Isle in Nod-Krai. It holds experiments on kuuvahki, the lunar energy, and collects data from three surface hubs to study how to generate high-density energy barriers.

The Traveler finds it through the world quest Priorities First (Version 6.0). It is a Strong Kuuvahki Environment. A notice there says Command raised the alert level because of recent suspicious activity around the Design Bureau, to protect military secrets and personnel.

Geography: The center is reached from the Paha Isle surface by an entrance and a long elevator shaft that descends well underground. The first area has a sealed barrier and moving barrier traps, and a further elevator leads deeper to the laboratory.

Places: The laboratory holds many jars of what looks like kuuvahki, a large jar in the center, piles of papers and experiment machines. Notices and notes here include an alert from Command raising the security level, a research log and a set of research records, all describing barrier tests.

People: Only unseen researchers are present; one log writer complains about sharing a space with those who tinker with plants and animals. The Fatui officer Kholodov, a Podporuchik, arrives with soldiers when the party submits the data, and accuses them of being the criminals who ruined an experiment site.

Quests: In Priorities First, the party gathers three data cassettes from the surface hubs, enters the lab and submits them. A large barrier traps them inside and Kholodov's Fatui attack; the Traveler breaks the barrier and defeats them. Afterwards the machine shows no result, and a white Weasel Thief steals Paimon's Mora.

Dangers: Sealed and moving barriers, the Cutting Edge All-Purpose Storm Landcruiser at the entrance, Force Recon Scout Landcruisers around the data hubs, and the Fatui who arrive when the data is submitted.

Atmosphere: A sunless place of glass jars, machines and dry bureaucratic notes. Paimon jokes that the lack of sunlight is meant to stop workers from knowing when to clock off.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it remains a Fatui research facility; the quest's results were never revealed.

202.comment: Underground Research Center: Data Storage Cassettes
202.content: The three data collection hubs on Paha Isle store experiment data on cassettes. The Traveler collects them and inputs them into the lab's computer. The data tracks high-density energy barrier generation; submitting it triggers a barrier that traps the party inside.

203.content: Kholodov is a Podporuchik of the Fatui who commands the soldiers that trap the party in the lab. He is angry because the Traveler had ruined an experiment site, and he is defeated in combat. The wiki does not give further background.

204.content:
Ungien's Circle (also: Ungien Biosphere, Sanctuary of Life, Bad-Uru-Namu-Ungien's biosphere): Ungien's Circle is a living biosphere built on the Frost Moon by the dragon life scientist Bad-Uru-Namu-Ungien. Seen from space it is a yellowed crater, and inside it plants, creatures and the kuuhenki thrive while the rest of the moon is barren and storm-lashed. It was a home for living beings on the moon, and it is where the Traveler and Eggie learn what became of Ungien (Visitors From the Stars, 6.7).

Its loading-screen description calls it a place holding Ungien's conviction, later passed on to the mistress of the greenhouse. A giant tree grows at its heart, and above it floats the Space Lifeform Capture Station.

Geography: The only region of the Frost Moon not subject to the low-gravity effects of turbulent Archaeolune Energy. Its landscape includes a large tree, vine-choked turbines, a Power Engine that must be restarted, a Transit Station with a waypoint, and a Skymount lift to the Space Lifeform Capture Station in orbit overhead. Moonlit Vines and Knotted Moonlit Vines grow thickly; kuuhenki, including Wondrous Black Kuuhenki, live there.

Places: Ungien's Circle: Power Engine (the turbines whose vines the Traveler clears), Ungien's Circle: Transit Station (waypoint), the Skymount (elevator) and the Space Lifeform Capture Station above. The last station contains a main observation room with a model showing Teyvat and its three moons, a gravity control room, the capture arm and the wreck of the Moongazer, the dragons' ship.

History: Ungien, a dragon life scientist and the pupil of Ibni-Belum, built the biosphere. He and his partner Maagees-Geti worked on the Frost Moon. After the Eye of Ibni-Belum recorded a new deep-space signal, Ungien flew the Moongazer to find its source. He returned fused with a creature from space, a data-based lifeform carrying a message of hope from a dying civilisation. He delivered the message and died. Maagees used an experimental method to convert him into an enormous kuuhenki of pure Archaeolune Energy, called Ungie.

Atmosphere: A sheltered pocket of life in an otherwise stormy, low-gravity moon: overgrown vines, great dragon machines and kuuhenki, with normal gravity underfoot.

Quests: Visitors From the Stars (Part 1) leads the Traveler and Eggie here by transit lane, helps kuuhenki fend off monsters, restores the power engine and ends at the Skymount. Part 2 reveals Ungien's fate. The Circle also appears in Project Moongazer (Part 2), where Columbina names it as one of the stops on the path of the project.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Circle still stands, its machinery working, vines cleared from the turbines, and kuuhenki living in it.

205.content: Ungien was a dragon life scientist of the Frost Moon; Maagees-Geti was his partner and fellow researcher. After his death delivering a message from a dying civilisation, Maagees transformed what remained of him into Ungie, a huge artificial kuuhenki. Their pupil Lusalim later collated the group's research. Both are named as benefactors by Nin-Kiggia's recording in Project Moongazer (Part 2).

206.comment: Ungien's Circle: Space Lifeform Capture Station
206.content: An orbital station above Ungien's Circle where Ungien intended to hold creatures from space. The Traveler reaches it by the Skymount and is weightless inside; the Moongazer lies wrecked there.

207.content:
Vesnici Proleca Greenhouse: The Vesnici Proleca Greenhouse is a flower shop in Nasha Town, Nod-Krai, run by Richeza.

It sells local specialties and cooking ingredients, and Richeza's stock restocks every three days.

People: Richeza is the employee who runs the shop and its vendor; Viljami is also listed at the location.

Status as of 7.1: Operating as of 7.1; no change recorded.

208.content:
Voidsea Outlook: Voidsea Outlook is the area at the southern end of Pohjola, the large northern island of Nod-Krai, north of Paha Isle (added in 6.3). It holds Piramida, the mountain city that is the headquarters of the Lightkeepers, and Dreadshade Mire, a fog-choked swamp where an ancient Abyssal evil is sealed behind three stone pillars.

Together with the Southern Isles, Piramida is one of the most populated places in Nod-Krai. The area mixes a living, watchful military city with a hazardous swamp the Lightkeepers have posted warnings around.

Geography: Voidsea Outlook lies at Pohjola's southern edge, facing the Southern Isles across the water. Piramida stands on a mountain around a huge lighthouse; Dreadshade Mire spreads as a swamp whose thick fog limits visibility and is edged with warning signboards.

Places: Piramida: a city built atop an ancient castle; Lightkeeper headquarters. Dreadshade Mire: a fog-shrouded swamp, the prison of the Serpent of All Evils.

People: The Lightkeepers: volunteer soldiers called Ratniki under squad leaders, sergeant majors and the Starshyna (currently Nikita), who is based in Piramida. In the swamp, Lightkeeper observers such as Janusz and Oskari appear in the world quest.

Governance: Piramida is the seat of the Lightkeepers, an order founded 500 years ago by royal edict of Anastasya as an autonomous military body within Nod-Krai. Command runs from the Starshyna through Sergeant Majors to Squad Leaders and Ratniki. Because the order is stretched thin, outsiders sometimes view its headquarters as aloof, and relaying information to it is said to be hard.

Culture: Lightkeeper culture centres on the vow to keep a light burning in the long night: a nightingale holding a burning wick is their traditional insignia. Banquets in the mead hall celebrate victories and honour the fallen; by long custom the first pour of the feast is offered to the dead.

History: Piramida was built atop the ancient ruins of Prokhor Trubetskoy's castle, with a giant golden-age lighthouse at its centre. The Lightkeepers have made it their headquarters since their founding by Solovei. Dreadshade Mire is where Solovei and Aila, the first Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions, imprisoned the Serpent of All Evils with three ancient stone seals.

Atmosphere: Piramida: a tiered mountain city under a vast sky, the beacon of the lighthouse, long tables and the statue overhead; a feeling of old duty and fellowship. Dreadshade Mire: grey fog, dead water, glowing sealing pillars and the sense of being watched.

Dangers: Dreadshade Mire is marked by Lightkeeper notice signs as extremely dangerous; entry is discouraged because of low visibility and roaming Wild Hunt creatures. Elite enemies include Fishers of Hidden Depths, Wilderness Exiles and Radiant Glacial Wolves; pale-furred wolves and Treasure Hoarders are the ordinary threats.

Quests: To Turn Each Sin Against the Sinner (world quest, 6.3): in Dreadshade Mire the Traveler investigates three sealing pillars and defeats the Serpent of All Evils. Nightingale's Song, the Nod-Krai quest series, also uses Piramida.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the area is open; the Serpent of All Evils has been defeated in the world quest, and Piramida remains the Lightkeepers' stronghold.

After Nightingale's Song, Piramida appears in a different state from before. Nothing in 7.0-7.1 is recorded as changing the area.

209.content: Piramida is the city of the Lightkeepers, built on a mountain around a giant golden-age lighthouse. Its namecard line reads that in the blackest of nights, a lamp shall rise. A statue of Solovei the Torchforger stands in it; a mead hall at its top holds the Lightkeepers' feasts.

210.content: Dreadshade Mire is a fog-shrouded swamp where Solovei, the Torchforger, and Aila, first Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions, sealed the Serpent of All Evils with three ancient stone seals. Lightkeeper signboards warn that entry is not advised.

211.content:
Wavechaser Plain: Wavechaser Plain is the central, coastal plain of Pohjola, the large island of northern Nod-Krai (added in 6.3). It holds the Pillar of Embla, a tower that the scholar Rotwang built to break the sky, the Knights of Favonius outpost Favonius Keep, the lake Amsvartnir and the barrier islands of the Wing of Keres.

Past and present sit side by side here: an Abyssal tower from the Cataclysm, Frostmoon Scion relics, and the tents of Mondstadt's knights, whose Grand Master's expedition made camp in Nod-Krai.

Geography: A wide plain beside the sea in the middle of Pohjola, bordered by Voidsea Outlook to the south and Ashveil Peak to the north. The Pillar of Embla rises from it, Lake Amsvartnir lies north of Piramida, and the Wing of Keres is a chain of barrier islands off the western side.

Places: Pillar of Embla: a divine pillar rooted in the earth and reaching skyward, built by Rauthvangi. Favonius Keep: the Knights' camp. Lake Amsvartnir: a lake with a sacred forest and a legend of a hidden court. Wing of Keres: barrier islands with Verdant Crests and other Frostmoon Scion artifacts.

People: Favonius Keep is staffed by the Knights of Favonius Expedition Team: Garrison Commander Anselm and Knights including Ekbert, Erminie, Laurent, Leifhelm, Nannina and Winfried; Godwin joins after Varka's story quest.

Governance: No local government. The Knights of Favonius run the Keep as an expeditionary garrison, and Lightkeepers watch the surroundings.

History: Five hundred years ago, during the Cataclysm, Rauthvangi (known at the Belyi Tsar's court as Rotwang) came to Nod-Krai and raised the Pillar of Embla to reach the false sky and open the way to the Abyss, which he called his 'Elysium'. The Scourge of Endless Decay aided him. According to Frostmoon Scion records, Aila went to the pillar at Solovei's request and ended the Abyssal catastrophe.

Atmosphere: Salt wind off the sea, a tall pillar dominating the skyline, ruined stone, the smell of dandelion wine at the Keep and the sense of old failures. The Lost Notes' tone is exhausted and conflicted: the writer doubts whether the campaign saves people or merely kills.

Dangers: Wild Hunt and Abyssal enemies, Abyssal Riftlines and Fog Barriers around the pillar, and, among the Wing of Keres islands, Evil Eye of Blightseep puzzles. Pale-furred wolves roam Amsvartnir.

Quests: Tower of Inversion (world quest, Nightingale's Song Act I, part 2; 6.3): the Traveler and Illuga enter the Pillar of Embla, purify its core and restore its barrier cores. It leads into When War Songs Rise in Ashveil Peak. Echoes of a Forsaken Song, the quest that unlocks the Ancient Handwriting, also touches the lake.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the plain is open to explore; the Pillar of Embla has been cleansed and the Knights' camp remains.

Varka returned to Mondstadt in 6.4 but still travels to the outpost. Nothing in 7.0-7.1 is recorded as changing the plain.

212.content: A tower built by Rauthvangi (Rotwang) to reach the false sky and ascend to his 'Pitch-black Elysium'. Aila ended the catastrophe at Solovei's request, 500 years ago, and the pillar still shapes its surroundings. It appears in a corrupted and a cleansed form.

213.content: The Knights of Favonius' outpost and expedition camp in Nod-Krai, with a large tent as its Meeting Point. Its map text describes warm dandelion-wine-scented breezes and a quote about stories gathering wherever people live.

214.content: A lake north of Piramida, above which the Royal Court of the Seelie is said to lie. Legend says whoever breaks the golden branch in the lake's sacred forest finds the court, which is hidden from mortal eyes by day.

215.content: The barrier islands on the western side of Wavechaser Plain, decorated with Verdant Crests and other Frostmoon Scion artifacts. The name probably alludes to the winged death spirits of Greek myth (an editor's note, not stated in the game).

216.content:
Wing of Keres: Wing of Keres is the name for the barrier islands on the western side of Wavechaser Plain in Nod-Krai. They are decorated with Verdant Crests and other artifacts of the Frostmoon Scions. A buried time capsule written by Hyperborean engineers is the main thing to find there.

The islands are a place for exploration: free kuuhenki, ride Moonlanes and solve Abyss and kuuvahki puzzles. The wiki suggests the name alludes to the keres of Greek myth.

Geography: A string of barrier islands off the western shore of Wavechaser Plain, within Pohjola. Winter Icelea grows here, and the islands are connected by Moonlanes, with kuuhenki in the north, west and south.

History: No local history of the islands themselves is given in the pages read. The Verdant Crests and Frostmoon Scion artifacts imply the Scions' presence, and a letter buried in a time capsule shows that Hyperborean people also left something here.

Quests: A Distant Dream of Elysium (unofficial name, hidden exploration objective, 6.3): free three kuuhenki in any order, then ride the Moonlane, which completes the objective (chests and the achievement The Mound in the Moonlight). Afterwards the mound of dirt near the chests can be examined to read the Letter Buried in the Time Capsule.

Dangers: Evil Eyes of Blightseep and a small group of hilichurls, including a Blazing Axe Mitachurl, in the north.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the islands are an unpopulated exploration site; the time capsule has been unearthed.

Nothing in the pages read changes their state through 7.1.

key: Letter Buried in the Time Capsule
217.comment: Wing of Keres: Hyperborean Time Capsule
217.content: A letter buried at Wing of Keres by a Hyperborean author, addressed to a successor in a far brighter era. Written in the tenth year of the Elysium Project, it describes a united civilisation led by Dawn's Navigator and the Exalted Saint, advanced Tekhneikos and Mekhaneikos, and hopes of reaching the true cosmos.

218.content:
The Witch's Garden (also: Witch's Garden, Wonderland in the Rabbit Hole): The Witch's Garden is a garden point of interest in Voidsea Outlook, Nod-Krai, introduced in version 6.3. It holds the Witch's Lodge, one of the secret homes of the Hexenzirkel mage Nicole, and has a Meeting Point of the same name beside a statue before the bridge. Its map description stresses that the garden's sculptures are ordinary and hold no time-stopping magic.

Visitors reach it through Nicole's Witch's Lodge world quest, which she presents as a tale about a grand mage called Nicola Coco. Over the following versions the lodge became a small treasure-hunt house with rooms that open one at a time. Nicole treats the place as both a hobby and a trap for the curious: help is offered to those who do their own work.

Geography: The garden lies in the Voidsea Outlook area of Nod-Krai, which the wiki locates at the southern end of the island Pohjola, north of Paha Isle. A bridge leads toward the lodge; the Meeting Point statue stands before it.

Places: The Witch's Lodge is the only listed point of interest inside the garden. The Meeting Point (level 5 unlocks a final Nicole conversation, Witch's Chatter) sits by the bridge-side statue.

People: Nicole is the only resident, and she is often absent. Post-quest lines have her say she is away (in one set, in Sumeru), leaving tea on the table; during The Lost Palace she says she is running a sculpture stall in Fontaine. Paimon and the Traveler are her usual guests.

History: The Witch's Garden opened with Luna IV (6.3, released 2026-01-14), together with its Witch's Lodge quest and Meeting Point. The hidden Beyond Silver and Fine Gold quest series, with new rooms, arrived with Luna VII (6.6, 2026-05-20), the same version as Nicole's release.

Quests: Witch's Lodge (6.3) opens the area; Witch's Chatter follows at Meeting Point level 5.
